title: ADR-0012: Verify JWT Access Tokens at the First API Boundary
heading: ADR-0012: Verify JWT Access Tokens at the First API Boundary
text:
ADR-0012: Verify JWT Access Tokens at the First API Boundary
**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-09-24

title: ADR-0012: Verify JWT Access Tokens at the First API Boundary
heading: Context
text:
Context
The Approval Request feature requires every operation to authenticate a human before applying ownership and review-capability rules. H-05 selected a provider-independent OIDC/OAuth 2.0 bearer access-token boundary and deferred a concrete identity provider, password/session systems, and provider-specific refresh and revocation behavior. Phase 5 must verify tokens in a running API and in synthetic tests without provisioning an external service.
The existing [authentication policy](../security/authentication.md) left the token format and cryptographic mechanism to an explicit decision. This choice affects security and issuer interoperability beyond a local helper implementation.

title: ADR-0012: Verify JWT Access Tokens at the First API Boundary
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
For the first Orion API, accept signed JWT bearer **access tokens** with `typ` of `at+jwt`, verified locally using the configured trusted issuer's JWKS. Require an exact issuer and API audience, a non-expired token, an issued-at time, a subject, a stable Orion application-principal UUID claim, and an issuer-validated human actor claim. Accept RS256 or ES256 signatures. Map an issuer-validated `approval:review` scope to the application capability; no unverified client-supplied identity or capability reaches the domain/application layer.
Keep issuer, audience, JWKS endpoint, and runtime database URL in validated server-only configuration. The stable Orion principal ID is a provider-independent application contract: a later provider integration must preserve that ID across provider changes. No concrete provider, login/session store, introspection service, token issuance, or provider-specific revocation strategy is selected here. A later requirement for opaque tokens or a different trust mechanism needs a separate decision and compatibility review.

title: ADR-0012: Verify JWT Access Tokens at the First API Boundary
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
Local signature verification makes the boundary executable and testable with synthetic keys without depending on an external account or network call per business request. Explicit issuer/audience checks and an application-owned principal identifier keep authorization independent of provider-native claim types. A narrow algorithm allowlist and trusted JWKS reduce ambiguity in accepted credentials.
This accepts a JWT-shaped issuer contract for the first API. It does not establish JWT as a universal Orion credential format or decide browser login behavior.

title: ADR-0012: Verify JWT Access Tokens at the First API Boundary
heading: Alternatives Considered
text: Alternatives Considered

title: ADR-0012: Verify JWT Access Tokens at the First API Boundary
heading: Opaque-token introspection
text:
Opaque-token introspection
Introspection could support provider-side active-token checks but would require selecting and provisioning an external issuer/introspection service for Phase 5, contrary to the current provider deferral and offline synthetic-test requirement. It remains available if future revocation or provider constraints justify it.

title: ADR-0012: Verify JWT Access Tokens at the First API Boundary
heading: API-owned session or password store
text:
API-owned session or password store
This would add credential and lifecycle responsibilities that H-05 explicitly excludes from the API.

title: ADR-0012: Verify JWT Access Tokens at the First API Boundary
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0012: Verify JWT Access Tokens at the First API Boundary
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
Authentication can be exercised with signed synthetic tokens and a local JWKS endpoint; authorization tests need no real accounts.
Application and domain operations receive only a stable principal ID and capability set.

title: ADR-0012: Verify JWT Access Tokens at the First API Boundary
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
A future issuer must supply the required JWT profile, stable Orion principal mapping, human actor assertion, and review scope. Provider compatibility must be checked before production integration.
Local signature verification does not by itself provide immediate provider-side token revocation. Provider-specific revocation and session behavior remain deferred; short token lifetimes and operational controls must be assessed with a chosen provider.

title: ADR-0012: Verify JWT Access Tokens at the First API Boundary
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
Deployments using the Approval Request feature must supply separate runtime database credentials and trusted token issuer/audience/JWKS settings. Keys may rotate through JWKS. Provider provisioning, issuer claims, and secure configuration are tracked under [H-07](https://github.com/GabriellMDias/Orion/blob/v1.1.1/docs/human-actions.md#h-07) only when a real provider is selected.

title: ADR-0013: Keep AGENTS.md as the Agent-Neutral Instruction Source
heading: ADR-0013: Keep AGENTS.md as the Agent-Neutral Instruction Source
text:
ADR-0013: Keep AGENTS.md as the Agent-Neutral Instruction Source
**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-09-29

title: ADR-0013: Keep AGENTS.md as the Agent-Neutral Instruction Source
heading: Context
text:
Context
Orion is built and maintained by humans together with AI coding agents. Its foundation was developed with OpenAI Codex, and its instructions and tracking documents named Codex as the actor responsible for maintaining the plan and human actions. Orion must remain usable with other agents, including Claude Code and Gemini CLI, without becoming coupled to one model, vendor, or harness.
Each tool has its own discovery convention. Duplicating repository rules into `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, or similar files would create competing authorities that drift apart, contradicting the single-canonical-source principle in [contributing](../contributing.md#authored-meaning-and-generated-facts). The owner directed that `AGENTS.md` remain canonical, that tool-specific files be added only as thin compatibility layers, and that tool behavior be verified against current documentation rather than assumed.
Verification on 2026-09-29 established that Codex reads `AGENTS.md` natively from the project root down to its working directory, with a 32 KiB default combined limit; that Claude Code 2.1.277 and later reads `AGENTS.md` natively, including nested files on demand, unless a `CLAUDE.md` is present; and that Gemini CLI 0.61.0 reads `GEMINI.md` by default but loads the `AGENTS.md` hierarchy when `context.fileName` names it. [Agent instructions](../architecture/agent-instructions.md) records the detailed, reverifiable behavior.

title: ADR-0013: Keep AGENTS.md as the Agent-Neutral Instruction Source
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
The root `AGENTS.md` and its nested `AGENTS.md` files are Orion's only repository instruction source for every contributor and agent. Normative repository text assigns obligations to the responsibility, such as a contributor or an authorized coding agent, and names a specific tool only to describe that tool's behavior.
A tool that cannot discover `AGENTS.md` receives a minimal committed discovery adapter that points it at `AGENTS.md` and contains no instructions. Currently only Gemini CLI needs one: `.gemini/settings.json` sets `context.fileName` to `["AGENTS.md"]`. Orion commits no `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, or other instruction copy.
Portability constraints are enforced mechanically where practical: validation rejects competing instruction files, restricts the Gemini adapter to discovery, and keeps each root-to-directory instruction chain within the 32 KiB limit that all verified tools load completely. The root instructions require reading applicable nested files before editing because not every tool loads them automatically.

title: ADR-0013: Keep AGENTS.md as the Agent-Neutral Instruction Source
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
`AGENTS.md` is supported natively or through configuration by all three verified tools, so one hierarchy can serve them without copies. Native discovery is preferred to import-based shims: a `CLAUDE.md` containing `@AGENTS.md` would work, but it is unnecessary on current Claude Code and would suppress direct `AGENTS.md` discovery by default. Gemini offers no native `AGENTS.md` default, and its supported project setting is the smallest configuration that loads the canonical hierarchy.
Mechanical checks make the policy durable as tools and contributors change. Executable validation, not prompting, remains the authority for architecture and behavior.

title: ADR-0013: Keep AGENTS.md as the Agent-Neutral Instruction Source
heading: Alternatives Considered
text: Alternatives Considered

title: ADR-0013: Keep AGENTS.md as the Agent-Neutral Instruction Source
heading: Vendor-specific instruction files
text:
Vendor-specific instruction files
Maintaining `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` beside `AGENTS.md` would give each tool its preferred file, but the copies would drift and create ambiguity about which rule is authoritative.

title: ADR-0013: Keep AGENTS.md as the Agent-Neutral Instruction Source
heading: Import or symlink shims for every tool
text:
Import or symlink shims for every tool
`@AGENTS.md` imports or symlinked files keep one source, but they add files that current tools do not need. Symlinks are unreliable in Windows checkouts, and a committed `CLAUDE.md` changes Claude Code's default discovery. They remain options only for a tool that requires them.

title: ADR-0013: Keep AGENTS.md as the Agent-Neutral Instruction Source
heading: A tool-neutral instruction format generated into vendor files
text:
A tool-neutral instruction format generated into vendor files
Generating vendor files from another source would add tooling and generated artifacts without a benefit over the widely supported `AGENTS.md` convention.

title: ADR-0013: Keep AGENTS.md as the Agent-Neutral Instruction Source
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0013: Keep AGENTS.md as the Agent-Neutral Instruction Source
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
One instruction hierarchy serves humans and all verified agents.
Agent-specific wording no longer implies that only one tool may maintain the plan or human actions.
Validation detects accidental instruction copies and oversized instruction chains.

title: ADR-0013: Keep AGENTS.md as the Agent-Neutral Instruction Source
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Tool behavior changes over time, so the compatibility table must be reverified before changing adapters or relying on a tool.
Gemini CLI applies the project setting only in a trusted workspace, and user or organization settings outside the repository can still change what any tool loads.
Instructions must stay concise enough for the smallest verified combined limit.

title: ADR-0013: Keep AGENTS.md as the Agent-Neutral Instruction Source
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
Contributors using an older Claude Code version or a local `CLAUDE.local.md` must update or configure their client to read `AGENTS.md`; the repository does not add a workaround file.

title: ADR-0014: Derive Projects from Orion through Git Ancestry with Recorded Provenance
heading: ADR-0014: Derive Projects from Orion through Git Ancestry with Recorded Provenance
text:
ADR-0014: Derive Projects from Orion through Git Ancestry with Recorded Provenance
**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-09-29
**Superseded by:** [ADR-0015](0015-name-stable-orion-foundation-revisions-with-semantic-tags.md), only for the statement that no release or version scheme exists; the provenance and upgrade decision remains accepted
**Superseded by:** [ADR-0017](0017-start-derived-projects-from-a-clean-foundation-baseline.md), only for inheriting Orion's plan, human actions, and acceptance history, retaining the Approval Request reference implementation with a recorded disposition, and keeping the `@orion/*` package scope; the Git ancestry, provenance, remote protection, and upgrade decisions remain accepted

title: ADR-0014: Derive Projects from Orion through Git Ancestry with Recorded Provenance
heading: Context
text:
Context
Orion's purpose is to be a reusable foundation for real projects. Each real project must be an independent repository with its own `origin`, pull requests, CI history, human actions, product decisions, and releases, while the canonical `GabriellMDias/Orion` repository continues evolving as the upstream foundation. Projects need to know which Orion revision they contain and to adopt later Orion improvements without losing product changes.
The repository also contains state that cannot be inherited as true for a new repository: Orion's implementation plan and acceptance evidence describe how Orion itself was built, several completed human actions verified GitHub settings for the Orion repository only, and the Approval Request feature is an executable reference rather than a product requirement. The owner directed a workflow that preserves Git ancestry, protects the canonical repository from accidental product pushes, records machine-readable provenance, and keeps upgrades as reviewable changes.

title: ADR-0014: Derive Projects from Orion through Git Ancestry with Recorded Provenance
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
A project is derived from a clean, full clone of Orion by the repository's `pnpm orion:init-project` command. After verifying preconditions, the command commits the project's initial identity on top of Orion's history, renames the canonical remote to `orion-upstream`, disables pushing to it and fetching its tags, removes local branch tracking of it, and adds the project's repository as `origin`. It creates no remote repository and pushes nothing.
`.orion/project.json` is the versioned, schema-checked identity and provenance record. In Orion it describes the foundation. In a derived project it records the project identity, the canonical Orion repository, the immutable commit the project was initialized from, the Orion baseline currently integrated, and the disposition of the Approval Request reference implementation. The immutable Git commit is the foundation version; no separate release or version scheme is introduced.
Foundation-owned and project-owned state are separated by file. Orion's plan, human actions, and acceptance report remain inherited foundation history in projects; initialization creates project-owned `docs/project/implementation-plan.md` and `docs/project/human-actions.md` with pending actions for the project's own repository settings. Root instructions route implementation work to the project-owned files when the manifest describes a project. The foundation namespace (`@orion/*`, `ORION_*`, `orion_*` claims, and the CI check name) is not renamed.
The Approval Request slice is retained in derived projects as a recorded `reference` implementation, not a product requirement. The project owner later records `adopted` or `removed`; validation keeps the disposition coherent with the source tree and refuses a durable release while it is still `reference`.
Orion upgrades are ordinary branches that merge a chosen commit from `orion-upstream/main` with its history, resolve conflicts under review, regenerate derived artifacts, and pass validation. The recorded baseline is updated only after that commit is integrated, and validation requires it to be an ancestor of `HEAD`.

title: ADR-0014: Derive Projects from Orion through Git Ancestry with Recorded Provenance
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
Preserving ancestry lets Git compute the upstream changes after a baseline and perform three-way merges, which is the property that makes future upgrades practical. A GitHub template repository or a squashed snapshot would discard that ancestry and force every upgrade to become a manual diff-and-copy exercise. Keeping the canonical repository as a fetch-only remote retains that ancestry without letting ordinary `git push` or `git pull` cross the boundary.
A small manifest makes provenance machine-checkable in local validation and CI without inventing a release system. Commit ancestry is verifiable wherever full history is available, and the recorded baseline cannot claim unintegrated upstream work.
Separate project-owned files avoid conflicts that would otherwise recur on every upgrade while keeping Orion's evidence intact rather than rewriting it. Retaining the reference implementation avoids a brittle, multi-artifact deletion step during initialization; the release guard ensures it cannot silently become product behavior.

title: ADR-0014: Derive Projects from Orion through Git Ancestry with Recorded Provenance
heading: Alternatives Considered
text: Alternatives Considered

title: ADR-0014: Derive Projects from Orion through Git Ancestry with Recorded Provenance
heading: GitHub template repository
text:
GitHub template repository
Templates create an unrelated history. They make project creation easy but lose the shared ancestry that three-way upgrade merges need, and they record no provenance.

title: ADR-0014: Derive Projects from Orion through Git Ancestry with Recorded Provenance
heading: Fork or shared-history repository with Orion as origin
text:
Fork or shared-history repository with Orion as `origin`
Working directly from a fork or clone that still pushes to Orion risks product work reaching the canonical repository, couples project pull requests and settings to Orion, and blurs project and foundation history.

title: ADR-0014: Derive Projects from Orion through Git Ancestry with Recorded Provenance
heading: Automatic updater that overwrites or patches foundation files
text:
Automatic updater that overwrites or patches foundation files
An updater could replace foundation files mechanically, but it would silently overwrite product changes or resolve semantic conflicts without review. Upgrades are engineering changes and remain reviewable merges.

title: ADR-0014: Derive Projects from Orion through Git Ancestry with Recorded Provenance
heading: Deleting the reference implementation during initialization
text:
Deleting the reference implementation during initialization
A scripted removal would have to change application code, tests, migrations, generated OpenAPI/SDK/database references, documentation, and portal data together, and would conflict with every later Orion change to those files. Retaining it with a recorded, validated disposition is smaller and safer.

title: ADR-0014: Derive Projects from Orion through Git Ancestry with Recorded Provenance
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0014: Derive Projects from Orion through Git Ancestry with Recorded Provenance
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
Each project is independent while retaining a verifiable relationship to Orion.
Accidental pushes to the canonical repository fail locally, and upstream changes enter projects only through reviewed merges.
Provenance, inherited-state boundaries, and the reference implementation's status are explicit and checked.

title: ADR-0014: Derive Projects from Orion through Git Ancestry with Recorded Provenance
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Project history includes Orion's history, and upgrades can still conflict where projects change foundation files.
Remote protection is local Git configuration; each clone must run `pnpm orion:upstream`, and repository-level protections still require the project's own settings.
Squash or rebase merges of upgrades break the baseline check and must be avoided.

title: ADR-0014: Derive Projects from Orion through Git Ancestry with Recorded Provenance
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
Orion itself changes only by adding its foundation manifest, validation, and documentation; its history and completed evidence are preserved.
A future change to the manifest schema requires a new schema version and an upgrade path for existing projects.

title: ADR-0015: Name Stable Orion Foundation Revisions with Semantic Tags
heading: ADR-0015: Name Stable Orion Foundation Revisions with Semantic Tags
text:
ADR-0015: Name Stable Orion Foundation Revisions with Semantic Tags
**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-09-29
**Supersedes:** [ADR-0014](0014-derive-projects-from-orion-through-git-ancestry-with-recorded-provenance.md), only its statement that no release or version scheme exists

title: ADR-0015: Name Stable Orion Foundation Revisions with Semantic Tags
heading: Context
text:
Context
[ADR-0014](0014-derive-projects-from-orion-through-git-ancestry-with-recorded-provenance.md) established immutable commit SHAs and ancestry as derived-project provenance and deliberately introduced no release scheme. Before the first real GitHub-backed derivation exercise, people need recognizable stable foundation points and compatibility signals without weakening that technical identity or making every merge a release.

title: ADR-0015: Name Stable Orion Foundation Revisions with Semantic Tags
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
Stable Orion foundation releases use immutable annotated Git tags named `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The tag is a human-readable alias for one commit. MAJOR denotes an intentionally incompatible foundation contract or supported upgrade model; MINOR denotes backward-compatible capability; PATCH denotes compatible correction or hardening. Classification follows contract impact, not diff size or incidental merge conflicts. A GitHub Release may describe a tag but has no provenance role. Pre-release naming is deferred until needed.
Project manifests continue to record commit SHAs. Derivation, baseline recording, and upgrades continue to rely on commit identity and Git ancestry. This decision changes only ADR-0014's no-release-scheme statement; its provenance and upgrade mechanics remain accepted.

title: ADR-0015: Name Stable Orion Foundation Revisions with Semantic Tags
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
Commit SHAs provide exact, verifiable identity while stable tags let humans communicate known foundation points. Semantic labels signal expected compatibility for projects that inherit and extend the foundation. Tags avoid a second mutable version store and do not require release automation or changes to project manifests. A stable-only model matches the current need for one first release; pre-release process would add obligations without an acceptance use case.

title: ADR-0015: Name Stable Orion Foundation Revisions with Semantic Tags
heading: Alternatives Considered
text: Alternatives Considered

title: ADR-0015: Name Stable Orion Foundation Revisions with Semantic Tags
heading: Continue with commit SHAs alone
text:
Continue with commit SHAs alone
This preserves exact identity but makes stable foundation points and compatibility intent difficult to communicate during the first real derivation and later upgrade exercise.

title: ADR-0015: Name Stable Orion Foundation Revisions with Semantic Tags
heading: Store a semantic version in project provenance
text:
Store a semantic version in project provenance
This duplicates the tag and could be mistaken for proof that the corresponding commit was integrated. The existing SHA and ancestry checks already supply that proof.

title: ADR-0015: Name Stable Orion Foundation Revisions with Semantic Tags
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0015: Name Stable Orion Foundation Revisions with Semantic Tags
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
Stable foundation points become easy to name without changing derivation mechanics.
The tag is a single human-readable release identifier; commit identity stays authoritative for provenance.

title: ADR-0015: Name Stable Orion Foundation Revisions with Semantic Tags
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Maintainers must classify contract impact deliberately and protect published tags from movement.
Version labels cannot predict merge conflicts caused by project-specific edits to shared files.

title: ADR-0015: Name Stable Orion Foundation Revisions with Semantic Tags
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
No manifest migration or release tooling is required. The first tag follows review, merge, and CI verification of this policy. Later tags are assigned only at deliberate release points.

title: ADR-0016: License the Orion Foundation under Apache-2.0
heading: ADR-0016: License the Orion Foundation under Apache-2.0
text:
ADR-0016: License the Orion Foundation under Apache-2.0
**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-09-30

title: ADR-0016: License the Orion Foundation under Apache-2.0
heading: Context
text:
Context
Orion is a public reusable development foundation intended for independent projects, including commercial and proprietary products. Its source had no explicit repository license through the `v1.0.0` foundation snapshot. The owner has now selected a distribution license for Orion source before the real GitHub-backed project derivation exercise. This is a durable repository-wide permission decision; it does not select a derived project's overall license or change third-party dependency rights.

title: ADR-0016: License the Orion Foundation under Apache-2.0
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
Distribute Orion's repository source under the unmodified Apache License, Version 2.0. The root `LICENSE` file contains the canonical terms, and the root README links to it. Do not retroactively change the existing `v1.0.0` tag. Orion's independently developed future revisions inherit this repository license unless a separately authorized decision changes it. Derived projects must make their own decisions for independently created product code and comply with licenses applicable to inherited and third-party material.

title: ADR-0016: License the Orion Foundation under Apache-2.0
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
The owner explicitly selected Apache-2.0 for broad reuse, modification, and distribution of the foundation, including use in independent commercial projects. A standard license file makes those permissions and obligations discoverable without custom terms, package publication metadata, or changes to derivation provenance. The existing `v1.0.0` tag remains an immutable record of the pre-license snapshot.

title: ADR-0016: License the Orion Foundation under Apache-2.0
heading: Alternatives Considered
text: Alternatives Considered

title: ADR-0016: License the Orion Foundation under Apache-2.0
heading: Leave the repository without an explicit license
text:
Leave the repository without an explicit license
This was the previous state. It leaves reuse and distribution permissions unclear for the intended audience, so it does not meet the owner's distribution objective.

title: ADR-0016: License the Orion Foundation under Apache-2.0
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0016: License the Orion Foundation under Apache-2.0
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
Orion source has a clear, standard distribution license.
Derived projects can identify the terms of inherited Orion material without changing SHA-based provenance or upgrade mechanics.

title: ADR-0016: License the Orion Foundation under Apache-2.0
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Redistributors must satisfy applicable Apache-2.0 conditions for Orion material; choosing a different license for their own code does not remove those obligations.
The root license does not settle separate rights or obligations for package dependencies or independently created project code.

title: ADR-0016: License the Orion Foundation under Apache-2.0
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
No manifest, package publication, application, or deployment change is required. The licensing change is a compatible PATCH candidate after PR review, merge, and CI verification. No `NOTICE` or copyright holder statement is added without supporting repository evidence.

title: ADR-0017: Start Derived Projects from a Clean Foundation Baseline
heading: ADR-0017: Start Derived Projects from a Clean Foundation Baseline
text:
ADR-0017: Start Derived Projects from a Clean Foundation Baseline
**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-09-30
**Supersedes:** [ADR-0014](0014-derive-projects-from-orion-through-git-ancestry-with-recorded-provenance.md), only for inheriting Orion's plan, human actions, and acceptance history, retaining the Approval Request reference implementation with a recorded disposition, and keeping the foundation workspace package scope; its Git ancestry, provenance, remote protection, and upgrade decisions remain accepted

title: ADR-0017: Start Derived Projects from a Clean Foundation Baseline
heading: Context
text:
Context
ADR-0014 derived projects through Git ancestry and kept everything Orion contained. A project therefore started with Orion's own implementation plan, human actions, and acceptance report as "inherited history", with the Approval Request slice as a retained reference implementation awaiting a product decision, and with `@orion/*` workspace packages. The first real derivation showed the cost: a new product repository read as Orion itself, carried documentation describing how Orion was built, and shipped an unrelated feature through its API, database, SDK, web application, and portal.
The owner directed that a new project start as a clean base for developing a product: it keeps Orion's architecture, principles, tooling, validation, CI, Living Documentation Portal, provenance, and future upgrades, but contains neither the reference implementation nor documentation of the foundation's development, and it carries the project's own name on its important surfaces.
Two structural facts made removal brittle under ADR-0014: shared runtime code imported the reference feature directly, and shared documentation linked to foundation-only files. A deletion step would have had to rewrite shared files and would conflict on every upgrade.

title: ADR-0017: Start Derived Projects from a Clean Foundation Baseline
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
Orion separates its content into three categories, recorded in the machine-readable derivation contract `.orion/derivation.json`:
**Shared foundation**: architecture, policies, ADRs, tooling, CI, the API runtime and module contract, the web shell and portal, and generated-reference machinery. Shared code and documentation must work without foundation-only content: they do not import, link to, name, or describe it. Validation in Orion enforces this isolation.
**Foundation-only**: Orion's Approval Request reference implementation (feature code, schema, migration, metadata, grants, smoke, tests, browser journeys, and domain documentation) and Orion's own implementation plan, human actions, and acceptance history.
**Project-owned**: files every repository owns from its first commit, rendered from templates at initialization: the README, the API and web composition files (`apps/api/src/modules.ts`, `apps/web/src/modules.tsx`), the brand assets, and `docs/project/implementation-plan.md` and `docs/project/human-actions.md`. Orion's own copies compose the reference implementation and describe Orion.
`pnpm orion:init-project` removes the foundation-only paths, renders the project-owned files from the project identity, renames the workspace package scope (package manifests, the lockfile, and source; not authored prose) to the project's scope, names the root package after it, regenerates every derived artifact from the changed sources, and records manifest schema version 2 with the project name and package scope. It then commits on top of Orion's history and protects the upstream remote exactly as ADR-0014 decided. Living Documentation titles, the HTML title, the OpenAPI title, and the telemetry service name derive from the manifest name and package names.
Upgrades remain reviewed merges with ancestry. Because the project deleted foundation-only paths, an upgrade that changes them conflicts or reintroduces them; `pnpm orion:prune` reapplies the contract by removing those paths and renaming foundation scope references, and project validation fails while either remains. Project-owned files keep the project's version during upgrades.
The `ORION_*` configuration names, `orion_*` token claims and database role names, and the `Orion required gate` check name remain the foundation's technical namespace. Renaming them would touch shared files throughout the repository and conflict on every upgrade, and the check name is bound to branch protection.

title: ADR-0017: Start Derived Projects from a Clean Foundation Baseline
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
Isolating shared content from foundation-only content turns removal into deleting a known list of paths rather than editing shared files, so a derived project shares every shared file byte for byte with Orion and upgrades merge cleanly there. Composition files give each repository a single owned seam for its modules; keeping Orion's reference behind that seam keeps it executable and validated in Orion, where it remains the example a project can study upstream.
A project that starts with Orion's history documents and a foreign feature must first remove or disclaim them, and its agents read another repository's plan as context. Starting clean makes the project's own plan and human actions the only current work and its README describe its actual state.
Renaming the package scope affects only package manifests, the lockfile, and a few imports, so it costs little at upgrade time and removes the most visible remaining Orion identity; `pnpm orion:prune` reapplies it mechanically. The configuration and claim namespaces appear in far more shared files and external configuration and are documented as foundation names instead.

title: ADR-0017: Start Derived Projects from a Clean Foundation Baseline
heading: Alternatives Considered
text: Alternatives Considered

title: ADR-0017: Start Derived Projects from a Clean Foundation Baseline
heading: Keep the reference implementation with a recorded disposition
text:
Keep the reference implementation with a recorded disposition
ADR-0014's model. It keeps initialization simple but makes every new product carry and validate an unrelated feature until someone performs a multi-artifact removal, which is exactly the brittle step this decision eliminates.

title: ADR-0017: Start Derived Projects from a Clean Foundation Baseline
heading: Delete the reference implementation by editing shared files during initialization
text:
Delete the reference implementation by editing shared files during initialization
A script could rewrite shared code and documentation, but every edited shared file would then differ from Orion and conflict on later upgrades. Isolation moves those differences into project-owned composition files instead.

title: ADR-0017: Start Derived Projects from a Clean Foundation Baseline
heading: Move the reference implementation to a separate repository or a non-default branch
text:
Move the reference implementation to a separate repository or a non-default branch
This would keep Orion's main branch clean but lose the executable example in the foundation's own validation gate, and projects could no longer see in Orion how a complete module fits the architecture.

title: ADR-0017: Start Derived Projects from a Clean Foundation Baseline
heading: Rename every Orion namespace
text:
Rename every Orion namespace
Renaming configuration variables, token claims, database roles, and the CI check would maximize branding but touch most of the repository and external settings, making every upgrade conflict.

title: ADR-0017: Start Derived Projects from a Clean Foundation Baseline
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0017: Start Derived Projects from a Clean Foundation Baseline
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
A new project contains only shared foundation content and its own files; its README, plan, human actions, package names, portal, and API contract describe it.
Orion keeps a complete, validated reference implementation and its development history.
Isolation, project cleanliness, and remaining foundation scope references are checked mechanically.

title: ADR-0017: Start Derived Projects from a Clean Foundation Baseline
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Upgrades that change foundation-only paths conflict in projects, and every upgrade must run `pnpm orion:prune` before validation.
Initialization regenerates references, so it requires dependencies installed and a Testcontainers-compatible container runtime.
Shared documentation cannot refer to the reference implementation except through the derivation guide.

title: ADR-0017: Start Derived Projects from a Clean Foundation Baseline
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
This changes the derivation contract and the manifest schema incompatibly, which [foundation versioning](../versioning.md#compatibility-meaning) classifies as a MAJOR foundation change.
Projects derived under ADR-0014 have a schema version 1 manifest; `pnpm orion:check` refuses it with directions to the migration steps in the [derivation guide](../project-derivation.md#migrate-a-project-from-schema-version-1).

title: ADR-0018: Propose Tenant-Owned Data in the Modular Backend
heading: ADR-0018: Propose Tenant-Owned Data in the Modular Backend
text:
ADR-0018: Propose Tenant-Owned Data in the Modular Backend
**Status:** proposed
**Date:** 2026-10-17

title: ADR-0018: Propose Tenant-Owned Data in the Modular Backend
heading: Context
text:
Context
Teluni requires independent customer companies with branches, memberships, media and devices. The derived repository has PostgreSQL infrastructure and composable API modules but no product tables or tenant enforcement. Tenant isolation must exist in the first product slice, within Orion's modular backend boundaries.

title: ADR-0018: Propose Tenant-Owned Data in the Modular Backend
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
Propose one customer company as the tenant ownership boundary in a shared PostgreSQL database and schema. Model explicit tenant-scoped ownership and references, server-derived membership/branch authorization, and database constraints that prevent cross-tenant associations. Keep capabilities in the existing modular backend, with explicit application interfaces and owned tables; no microservice split is proposed.
Row-level security is an additional option to evaluate, not assumed protection. Review its connection-pooling, runtime-role and migration implications before selecting it. Platform administration remains a separate scoped capability, not an implicit bypass for tenant data access.

title: ADR-0018: Propose Tenant-Owned Data in the Modular Backend
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
A shared deployment fits the initial cost and operational constraints. Explicit ownership allows branch scoping and future company scale without treating a branch as another tenant. It also places substantial responsibility on query/reference design, constraints and adversarial authorization tests; the proposal has not yet been proven by a schema or implementation.

title: ADR-0018: Propose Tenant-Owned Data in the Modular Backend
heading: Alternatives Considered
text:
Alternatives Considered
**Database or schema per company:** provides a different isolation boundary, but adds migration, connection, backup and recovery coordination for every tenant. Revisit if contractual isolation or measured scale justifies it.
**Application filters without relational tenant constraints:** simpler initially, but insufficient to protect mixed-tenant references or accidental omitted scope checks. Not a sufficient candidate for the product requirement.

title: ADR-0018: Propose Tenant-Owned Data in the Modular Backend
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0018: Propose Tenant-Owned Data in the Modular Backend
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
Preserves one operational backend while giving each module clear ownership and tenant semantics.
Enables negative integration tests against real PostgreSQL from the first vertical slice.

title: ADR-0018: Propose Tenant-Owned Data in the Modular Backend
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Every data access, reference, cache, media path and asynchronous operation must preserve scope.
Isolation in a shared database requires continuing review; application administrator access and recovery operations remain sensitive.

title: ADR-0018: Propose Tenant-Owned Data in the Modular Backend
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
No tables or migrations are introduced by this proposal. Acceptance requires an ownership/constraint design, role matrix and cross-tenant tests, including the decision on row-level security. Later changing tenant partitioning may require a deliberate data migration.

title: ADR-0019: Propose Immutable Publications and Atomic Player Activation
heading: ADR-0019: Propose Immutable Publications and Atomic Player Activation
text:
ADR-0019: Propose Immutable Publications and Atomic Player Activation
**Status:** proposed
**Date:** 2026-10-17

title: ADR-0019: Propose Immutable Publications and Atomic Player Activation
heading: Context
text:
Context
Teluni displays must continue through temporary backend/network outages. Videos must normally play locally. Partial downloads, concurrent publications and power loss must not replace usable programming with an incomplete set. Backend and installed players will evolve independently.

title: ADR-0019: Propose Immutable Publications and Atomic Player Activation
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
Propose immutable publication snapshots with versioned manifests that bind programming rules to verified asset versions. The player durably stages missing assets and switches its active generation only after the complete supported snapshot is ready, retaining a valid recovery generation. Separate desired, staged and reported-active versions and reconcile duplicate or lost acknowledgements.
Define protocol compatibility, integrity metadata, capacity/retention, scheduling expiry and offline authorization policy before implementation. No transport, storage library, cryptographic mechanism or manifest serialization format is selected by this record.

title: ADR-0019: Propose Immutable Publications and Atomic Player Activation
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
The owner's requirement is consistent offline playback, not normal continuous server streaming. A generation boundary makes interruption and recovery behavior testable and avoids exposing partially updated programming. This is a design proposal, not evidence of crash-safe storage or hardware compatibility.

title: ADR-0019: Propose Immutable Publications and Atomic Player Activation
heading: Alternatives Considered
text:
Alternatives Considered
**Continuous server streaming:** makes ordinary playback depend on connectivity and repeated transfer; does not satisfy the central offline requirement.
**Overwrite active files/programming as downloads arrive:** reduces temporary storage but can mix incompatible versions and leave no valid program after interruption. It does not satisfy the required activation boundary.

title: ADR-0019: Propose Immutable Publications and Atomic Player Activation
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0019: Propose Immutable Publications and Atomic Player Activation
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
Enables local replay through outages and explicit recovery/failure acceptance tests.
Separates publication intent from device observations without assuming exactly-once delivery.

title: ADR-0019: Propose Immutable Publications and Atomic Player Activation
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Staging plus recovery versions consume additional storage and need safe garbage collection.
Cached content cannot be immediately recalled from unreachable devices; expiry/revocation rules need explicit review.

title: ADR-0019: Propose Immutable Publications and Atomic Player Activation
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
Atomicity across PostgreSQL and media storage needs durable intent/reconciliation. The player needs proven local activation durability and a supported backend/player overlap. Acceptance requires representative network/power-cut and stale/reordered message cases, not only unit tests.

title: ADR-0020: Propose a Native Android TV Player
heading: ADR-0020: Propose a Native Android TV Player
text:
ADR-0020: Propose a Native Android TV Player
**Status:** proposed
**Date:** 2026-10-17

title: ADR-0020: Propose a Native Android TV Player
heading: Context
text:
Context
The intended first player is Android TV, with continuous image/video playback, local persistence, temporary-code pairing and offline recovery. Orion supplies TypeScript API/web foundations but deliberately does not select a mobile/native stack. No Android application or hardware validation exists in Teluni.

title: ADR-0020: Propose a Native Android TV Player
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
Propose an independently built/distributed native Android TV player using Kotlin and Android Media3/ExoPlayer, with durable local media/configuration/synchronization state. Consume versioned backend HTTP contracts; do not import backend or web implementation. Keep player credentials in reviewed platform-protected storage.
Minimum platform version, supported devices/codecs/orientations, persistence library, packaging, startup/unattended behavior and controlled update/rollback mechanisms remain pending validation. This proposal does not imply every Android TV or Smart TV is supported.

title: ADR-0020: Propose a Native Android TV Player
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
This is the owner's preferred initial direction and matches the requested native device lifecycle and local-playback responsibilities. There are no completed benchmarks or device tests establishing that it meets the reliability envelope. A separate runtime is justified by installation and hardware lifecycle, while backend distribution is not.

title: ADR-0020: Propose a Native Android TV Player
heading: Alternatives Considered
text:
Alternatives Considered
**Web player first:** remains a possible future platform, but browser lifecycle, storage and unattended playback would need separate validation. It is not the requested MVP target.
**Other Smart TV or dedicated-computer players:** could expand coverage later; validating multiple platforms now would widen MVP support and test obligations without pilot evidence.

title: ADR-0020: Propose a Native Android TV Player
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0020: Propose a Native Android TV Player
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
Gives the first player a clear device-specific owner and keeps interoperable contracts with Orion.
Allows targeted validation of local storage, playback and restart behavior on pilot hardware.

title: ADR-0020: Propose a Native Android TV Player
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Adds Android build/signing/distribution, hardware testing and old-client compatibility responsibilities.
Media capability and unattended behavior must be verified per supported device; TypeScript tooling cannot establish them.

title: ADR-0020: Propose a Native Android TV Player
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
Acceptance requires the pilot hardware matrix, chosen installation/update policy and playback/reboot/power-loss evidence. No application directory, Gradle project, dependency or signing credential is created in this documentation stage.

title: ADR-0021: Propose a Single-Host Pilot with Portable Persistent Storage
heading: ADR-0021: Propose a Single-Host Pilot with Portable Persistent Storage
text:
ADR-0021: Propose a Single-Host Pilot with Portable Persistent Storage
**Status:** proposed
**Date:** 2026-10-17

title: ADR-0021: Propose a Single-Host Pilot with Portable Persistent Storage
heading: Context
text:
Context
The owner currently has no cloud-service budget and intends to evaluate a personal residential server for development and first pilots. Network exposure, CGNAT, domain, hardware capacity, backup destination and acceptable downtime have not been verified. Orion does not select a production deployment platform.

title: ADR-0021: Propose a Single-Host Pilot with Portable Persistent Storage
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
Propose an initial Debian host with Docker Compose, HTTPS reverse-proxy ingress, private PostgreSQL and media on durable mounted storage outside disposable containers. Keep environment-specific endpoints/configuration out of domain identity. Media storage remains a cohesive capability with replaceable filesystem I/O, allowing a later S3-compatible implementation when justified.
Real-customer exposure is conditional on network/security review, owner-approved availability and recovery targets, off-host backup/restore proof and tested player behavior during outages. No tunnel, DNS, proxy, object-storage or cloud provider is selected or presumed to satisfy these gates.

title: ADR-0021: Propose a Single-Host Pilot with Portable Persistent Storage
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
One host and local media fit the stated budget and avoid premature distributed operations. Stable logical asset identity, explicit configuration and tested recovery make a host/storage move tractable. They do not remove single-host failure or bandwidth constraints, nor make a future migration automatic.

title: ADR-0021: Propose a Single-Host Pilot with Portable Persistent Storage
heading: Alternatives Considered
text:
Alternatives Considered
**Immediate paid VPS/cloud:** potentially changes power/network risk, but needs an actual affordable operating budget. Revisit with revenue or a demonstrated operational requirement.
**Distributed services or orchestration first:** adds deployment and failure-management costs without measured need at the initial pilot scope.

title: ADR-0021: Propose a Single-Host Pilot with Portable Persistent Storage
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0021: Propose a Single-Host Pilot with Portable Persistent Storage
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
Keeps the first operating model understandable and limits mandatory paid infrastructure.
Establishes persistent state and endpoint portability as design obligations before deployment.

title: ADR-0021: Propose a Single-Host Pilot with Portable Persistent Storage
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Residential availability, uplink and physical security remain material risks; no production SLA follows from Compose.
Database-plus-media consistency, off-host recovery, secure exposure and maintenance remain owner/operator responsibilities.

title: ADR-0021: Propose a Single-Host Pilot with Portable Persistent Storage
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
Acceptance requires the host/network inventory, endpoint migration strategy and timed recovery rehearsal. Implementation must later supply tested deployment/recovery runbooks and release procedures. No container manifest or production change is introduced here.

title: ADR-0022: License Teluni under Apache-2.0
heading: ADR-0022: License Teluni under Apache-2.0
text:
ADR-0022: License Teluni under Apache-2.0
**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-10-17

title: ADR-0022: License Teluni under Apache-2.0
heading: Context
text:
Context
Teluni is derived from Orion, whose source already carries Apache-2.0 under ADR-0016. That foundation decision explicitly leaves independently developed product licensing to the product owner. Teluni's owner explicitly approved Apache License 2.0 for Teluni on 2026-10-17; this record documents that owner-authorized decision. The repository already contains the standard root license text, but its README and human actions previously said product licensing was undecided.

title: ADR-0022: License Teluni under Apache-2.0
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
License Teluni repository source and documentation, including independently developed product material, under the unmodified Apache License, Version 2.0. Retain the root `LICENSE` as the canonical terms and use SPDX identifier `Apache-2.0` in the root, API, web and SDK package metadata. Update README and project documentation to make the scope explicit.
Preserve Orion provenance and its applicable rights/notices. Do not relabel third-party dependencies or separately licensed material. Do not invent a named copyright holder or NOTICE without confirmed attribution. This decision concerns repository licensing; SaaS pricing, support and customer service terms remain separate product decisions.

title: ADR-0022: License Teluni under Apache-2.0
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
The owner explicitly selected Apache-2.0 rather than delegating the legal choice to an agent. Applying the existing standard text consistently to Teluni resolves the previous distinction between inherited foundation licensing and undecided product licensing, without changing architecture or runtime behavior.

title: ADR-0022: License Teluni under Apache-2.0
heading: Alternatives Considered
text: Alternatives Considered

title: ADR-0022: License Teluni under Apache-2.0
heading: Keep product licensing undecided
text:
Keep product licensing undecided
This was the documented state. It no longer reflects the owner's explicit instruction and leaves the intended licensing scope unclear.

title: ADR-0022: License Teluni under Apache-2.0
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0022: License Teluni under Apache-2.0
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
Teluni's source/documentation license is explicit and consistent with the standard license file and package metadata.
The product decision remains separate from the historical Orion ADR and commercial pricing decisions.

title: ADR-0022: License Teluni under Apache-2.0
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Distribution must preserve applicable license/attribution obligations; the choice does not determine third-party rights or authorize reuse of PDT Display material.
Named attribution still needs confirmed ownership evidence if such notices are added.

title: ADR-0022: License Teluni under Apache-2.0
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
No database migration, dependency upgrade, application feature or deployment change is required. Existing tags/history and the canonical license text remain unchanged. PH-06 records the owner's selection; PH-14 tracks conditional named-attribution work.

title: ADR-0023: Propose Versioned Catalog and Composition Publications
heading: ADR-0023: Propose Versioned Catalog and Composition Publications
text:
ADR-0023: Propose Versioned Catalog and Composition Publications
**Status:** proposed
**Date:** 2026-10-18

title: ADR-0023: Propose Versioned Catalog and Composition Publications
heading: Context
text:
Context
The owner requires freeform simultaneous content, regional schedules with optional page coordination, multiple videos/audio and configurable data catalogs beyond products, such as weekly agendas. Saving designated prices must automatically publish affected content, while other drafts remain private. Players must render locally through bounded outages and recover complete valid generations.
These approved product policies affect schema evolution, references, module ownership and backend/web/player contracts. They do not choose a physical schema, editor/renderer, serialization or queue provider. ADR-0019 proposes immutable publication generations; the expanded presentation/data boundary needs explicit design review before implementation.

title: ADR-0023: Propose Versioned Catalog and Composition Publications
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
Propose versioned declarative composition definitions and typed catalog definitions/records with stable field/binding identities. Customization is validated data rather than executable user code or direct database access. Catalog presets may express products/prices or agendas without making a product schema mandatory for every collection.
Compose immutable publication snapshots from explicitly identified layout/schema/record/media revisions and the rules needed for offline evaluation. Published snapshots remain interpretable after draft schema evolution. A price save records durable intent and generates affected snapshots from published dependencies, excluding unrelated drafts; expose incomplete/retry states and prevent stale work from overwriting newer desired generations.
Keep catalogs, layout authoring, programming and publication behind explicit module capabilities in the modular backend. No arbitrary cross-module table writes, circular imports or new generic shared framework are implied. Carry interoperable contracts to the native player rather than importing TypeScript application internals.
Before acceptance/implementation, review concrete schemas, module collaboration, import security, destructive field evolution, snapshot granularity, trusted time, rendering/media profiles and the failure/compatibility fixtures. Serialization, storage layout, libraries and processing/transport mechanisms remain intentionally unselected.

title: ADR-0023: Propose Versioned Catalog and Composition Publications
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
User-defined fields and freeform geometry need stable meaning across independent editor/player releases. A versioned declarative boundary makes validation, copying, private references and offline rendering reviewable. Immutable data snapshots preserve the existing consistency/activation direction while allowing automatic price updates without live mutation of an issued program.
This is reasoned architecture, not a measured renderer/storage evaluation. Owner approval of PH-09 policies does not accept the technical proposal or establish product availability.

title: ADR-0023: Propose Versioned Catalog and Composition Publications
heading: Alternatives Considered
text:
Alternatives Considered
**Product-only fixed fields and opaque final artwork:** cannot satisfy configurable non-product catalogs, field-bound editing and independent regional presentation without rebuilding the model.
**Read mutable live records while rendering an old publication:** makes ordinary playback depend on the server or mixes data/layout/schema revisions; obscures rollback and offline commercial validity.
**Unversioned arbitrary catalog/layout objects:** initially flexible but leaves incompatible field changes, unsafe references and preview/player interpretation undefined. Extensibility still needs typed validation and compatibility rules.

title: ADR-0023: Propose Versioned Catalog and Composition Publications
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0023: Propose Versioned Catalog and Composition Publications
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
Supports sector-neutral catalogs, reusable textual layouts and controlled offline interpretation.
Keeps ordinary drafts separate from explicit automatic price publication and preserves attributable generation history.
Makes schema/reference/security and regional scheduling cases part of contract verification.

title: ADR-0023: Propose Versioned Catalog and Composition Publications
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Requires schema evolution/reference handling and qualified multi-area/video rendering across independent runtimes.
Publication fan-out, processing and retained generations add storage/work and recovery obligations.
Does not remove real device limits, trusted-time uncertainty or the inability to erase an unreachable player instantly.

title: ADR-0023: Propose Versioned Catalog and Composition Publications
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
No product schema or deployment currently exists, so this proposal adds no migration or running component. Future implementations must keep retained snapshots readable, reconcile interrupted price/publication work and qualify protocol overlap, offline/power recovery and supported device profiles. Review proposed ADR-0019 alongside this record; neither supersedes an accepted foundation decision.

title: ADR-0024: Propose Keycloak and Server-Managed Human Sessions
heading: ADR-0024: Propose Keycloak and Server-Managed Human Sessions
text:
ADR-0024: Propose Keycloak and Server-Managed Human Sessions
**Status:** proposed
**Date:** 2026-10-18

title: ADR-0024: Propose Keycloak and Server-Managed Human Sessions
heading: Context
text:
Context
The owner answered PH-11's identity questionnaire, selecting self-hosted Keycloak as candidate, email/password with optional passkeys, Google as the only external login, and server-managed browser sessions. Public company activation, strong administrative assurance, safe recovery and bounded revocation must work within an initially unfunded residential deployment. A concrete provider/version has not been provisioned or qualified.
Accepted ADR-0012 governs the existing API's signed JWT access-token boundary. Its header/claims are not ordinary provider defaults, and its current principal result does not expose session or authentication-assurance evidence. The web shell's in-memory bearer support is not a login/refresh implementation. This decision must distinguish product-policy approval from technical acceptance and implementation.

title: ADR-0024: Propose Keycloak and Server-Managed Human Sessions
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
Propose Keycloak as the human identity provider, self-hosted subject to PH-10 feasibility, with a server-managed browser session integrated into the modular backend where appropriate. Use established OIDC Authorization Code with PKCE and maintained session/security components; keep provider credentials server-side and an opaque protected session cookie in the browser. Do not introduce a new microservice by default or an API-owned password/cryptographic implementation.
Preserve ADR-0012's API boundary and stable application principal. A reviewed session boundary must obtain legitimate issuer access tokens and establish trusted session/assurance context; a cookie or caller-supplied MFA/session assertion cannot bypass the existing verifier. Define protected cookies, explicit CSRF protection, OIDC state/nonce/redirect validation, session fixation defenses, refresh rotation/replay/concurrency and local/global logout reconciliation before implementation. No session library, route, schema or provider version is selected by this proposal.
Apply the owner's canonical identity policies, including strong/recent authentication, distinct platform accounts, recovery, inactivity/absolute expiry, session-count and 30-second revocation requirements. Current account/session/membership state must supplement JWT verification. Keep Google brokering/account linking and provider/email credentials at trusted boundaries. A human actor mapper must not accidentally make machine flows authenticate as humans.
Before acceptance, review pinned-version compatibility, immutable principal mapping, every required token claim and trusted session/assurance linkage using the evidence/gaps in the provider evaluation. Where evidence is insufficient, retain an explicit qualification task; do not modify accepted checks to make a default provider token pass. Review deployment/recovery resources separately under PH-10/PH-15. This proposal neither supersedes ADR-0012 nor authorizes provisioning.

title: ADR-0024: Propose Keycloak and Server-Managed Human Sessions
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
The candidate matches the owner's control/budget direction and has relevant documented identity primitives. Server-managed sessions reduce browser exposure of provider tokens and permit accountable session lifecycle controls, at the cost of persistent state and CSRF/refresh coordination. A five-minute token alone cannot enforce the selected 30-second revocation bound. Local JWT verification can remain useful without pretending it provides a complete session or authorization system.
The documentation review establishes plausible compatibility, including Keycloak's configurable `at+jwt` header, not passed interoperability, recovery or capacity tests. Public signup still needs commercial/privacy and abuse readiness; choosing it does not authorize a free plan or immediate public exposure.

title: ADR-0024: Propose Keycloak and Server-Managed Human Sessions
heading: Alternatives Considered
text:
Alternatives Considered
**Managed OIDC provider:** may reduce some operating responsibilities, but costs/limits/claim compatibility require evaluation beyond the current no-procurement direction. No vendor benchmark or unconditional free-tier assumption is made.
**Browser-token SPA with Authorization Code and PKCE:** preserves a simpler server session topology but leaves browser token exposure and refresh/lifecycle tradeoffs; the owner selected server-managed sessions instead. This does not reject the client-first React/Vite application or require server rendering.
**Another established self-hosted provider:** fallback if qualification rejects Keycloak; no unperformed comparative assessment is claimed.
**Custom issuer/password storage or relaxed JWT checks:** violates governing controls and is not an acceptable workaround.

title: ADR-0024: Propose Keycloak and Server-Managed Human Sessions
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0024: Propose Keycloak and Server-Managed Human Sessions
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
Keeps human credentials with an established provider and browser tokens out of JavaScript-accessible persistence.
Preserves provider-independent identity and explicit failure/revocation/assurance boundaries.
Defines compatibility and operational evidence before a production integration is claimed.

title: ADR-0024: Propose Keycloak and Server-Managed Human Sessions
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Self-hosting adds patching, resources, recovery and mail-delivery responsibilities despite no procurement budget.
Server sessions introduce persistence, CSRF, concurrency and logout synchronization work.
Current foundation principal/configuration contracts do not yet carry all needed session/assurance semantics.

title: ADR-0024: Propose Keycloak and Server-Managed Human Sessions
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
No runtime, dependency, API contract, migration or deployment changes accompany this proposal. Future delivery must pin a maintained provider version/image, define protected credentials/configuration, qualify claim/assurance/session behavior and reconcile revocations on restore. Provider migration preserves application IDs but may require password resets or factor reenrollment. PH-15–PH-17 track external identity, Google and mail prerequisites; PH-11 technical acceptance remains open.

title: ADR-0025: Propose Application-Owned Scoped Access Profiles
heading: ADR-0025: Propose Application-Owned Scoped Access Profiles
text:
ADR-0025: Propose Application-Owned Scoped Access Profiles
**Status:** proposed
**Date:** 2026-10-18

title: ADR-0025: Propose Application-Owned Scoped Access Profiles
heading: Context
text:
Context
PH-11 approved multiple company memberships, branch-specific grants, customizable profiles and explicit resource sharing. A designated responsible administrator approves additional administrators. The backend must enforce the selected role matrix, strong authentication, 30-second revocation and publication impact, including automatically published prices. Company administration and platform operation must not imply unrestricted customer-content support.
The foundation verifies human identity but has no product membership/permission implementation. ADR-0018 proposes tenant-owned modular data; its physical enforcement remains unaccepted. Provider-native groups or immutable token roles alone cannot express current resource scope, temporary grants and all-target price effects safely.

title: ADR-0025: Propose Application-Owned Scoped Access Profiles
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
Propose application-owned memberships, explicit scoped capability grants and company-customized profiles, with readable standard role presets. Scope grants to a company and explicit branches/resources; combine valid grants additively within their scopes. Account/membership suspension and grant expiration deny access regardless of profile labels. No implicit access to future branches, arbitrary negative-rule language, cyclic inheritance or universal administrator shortcut is selected.
Keep authorization meaning with the owning application/module capabilities; identity/provider adapters establish trusted principals and assurance but do not own company permissions. The organizations capability owns membership/profile meaning. Modules use explicit public capabilities for authorization facts rather than arbitrary cross-module table reads or a generic global switch over domain rules. Exact schema, persistence constraints, caching/invalidation and any row-level-security design require review with ADR-0018 before implementation. No external permission engine or shared framework is selected.
Enforce resource ownership, operation, current state, assurance and scope on every protected entry point, including reads/collections, media, imports, bulk work and delayed effects. Revalidate sensitive effects and ensure the selected freshness bound. Grantors cannot delegate authority they lack, responsible-administrator approval cannot be bypassed, and local membership administration cannot reset global identities.
Authorize every published dependency/target affected by a price save before accepting the mutation; deny the entire out-of-scope mutation without partial publication or automatic approval fallback. Optional company approval policies distinguish a proposal from an effective saved price and prohibit self-approval where required. Pending protected work rechecks authority; an already-issued valid publication continues its delivery lifecycle unless explicitly revoked by the appropriate control.
Routine support uses the real support identity and a visible, expiring customer-authorized scope, read-only by default and separate write grants. No impersonation is selected. Emergency access requires a separately reviewed, exceptional controlled procedure; there is no standing unrestricted content-browsing right.

title: ADR-0025: Propose Application-Owned Scoped Access Profiles
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
Application ownership keeps mutable company permissions and resources independent of provider migration and stale identity claims. Explicit capabilities/scopes accommodate both small-business presets and teams working across branches without making every operator an administrator. Attributable publication/support checks preserve the approved product behavior and tenant boundaries.
The owner approved policy and required allow/deny cases, not a database model or proven permission evaluator. Custom profiles, optional approvals and bounded asynchronous revocation add real implementation work and must not be claimed merely from a matrix.

title: ADR-0025: Propose Application-Owned Scoped Access Profiles
heading: Alternatives Considered
text:
Alternatives Considered
**Fixed roles only:** simpler, but cannot satisfy the selected customizable capability/scoping policy without revisiting the product requirements.
**Provider roles/groups as complete authorization:** insufficient for current memberships, mutable resource relationships, publication fan-out and tenant-safe support; would couple application permission meaning to identity infrastructure.
**General-purpose policy engine:** no measured need or evaluation justifies another dependency or distributed component at this stage. Review if actual policy complexity warrants it later.
**Platform superuser and silent price partial success:** obscure authority and violate selected customer-content boundaries and complete price-impact validation.

title: ADR-0025: Propose Application-Owned Scoped Access Profiles
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0025: Propose Application-Owned Scoped Access Profiles
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
Makes granted authority, tenant/resource scope, responsibility and delegated support explainable and testable.
Keeps identity migration independent from company permission ownership.
Preserves safe all-target publication and attributable pending-work behavior.

title: ADR-0025: Propose Application-Owned Scoped Access Profiles
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Custom profiles, shared resources and optional approvals increase UX, schema and test complexity.
Freshness, grant races and background work require explicit consistency/invalidation design.
A safe role matrix alone cannot prevent unsafe queries, caches or credential mapping.

title: ADR-0025: Propose Application-Owned Scoped Access Profiles
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
No permission identifiers, schema, migration or running engine is created here. Acceptance needs reviewed capability ownership, consistency/enforcement design and IA-01–IA-16 cases, including two-company negative fixtures and trustworthy session/assurance context. Later renaming persisted grants or broadening presets is a compatibility/security change. Audit/privacy retention and host recovery remain separate gates.
